extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers (3–8 years post-PhD) applying for a Royal Society–SFI University Research Fellowship hosted in the Republic of Ireland (Trinity College Dublin applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting an application to the Royal Society–SFI University Research Fellowship (URF) scheme hosted at Trinity College Dublin, including eligibility, application components, formatting limits, budget instructions, and reviewer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility (research experience window)
rubrics_metrics.description: They must be in the early stages of their researcher career and must have between 3 and 8 years of research experience since their PhD (by the closing date of the round). Note that the date used to qualify the 3 years from the closing date of the call is the date when the applicant first took up a postdoc position and not the date of the award of the PhD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Royal Society supports non-traditional career paths (e.g., time spent outside academia counts appropriately if you returned to a research/postdoc-type position within the qualifying window). Read the Scheme Notes for full details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility (employment and nationality/work history)
rubrics_metrics.description: They must not hold a permanent post in a university or not-for-profit organisation in the European Economic Area (EEA). They must be a citizen of the EEA, a Swiss citizen or have worked in a research institution in the EEA in the last two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Scheme Notes for full information and contact the Royal Society if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration and funding components
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are awarded initially for 5 years, with the possibility of a further 3-year extension. Awards consist of fellow’s salary (at ‘Research Fellow’ level on SFI’s salary scales) and research costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example research costs given: €15,000 in year 1, €13,000 for subsequent years. The URF offers development activities (innovation course, media/communications training, URF conference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: Scientific merit of the individual
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific merit of the individual: past achievements, research career to date, publication record, likely contribution to research field, future potential, likelihood of independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the applicant’s track record and potential to become an independent, world-leading researcher; evidence of research achievements and trajectory is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: Host institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Host institution: suitability, appropriate expertise/equipment, research environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The host must demonstrate that it can provide the environment and resources needed for the fellow to succeed; justify choice of host and highlight unique institutional advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: Proposed research project
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed research project: quality and originality of proposed project, definition of research plan, likelihood of achieving goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project assessment focuses on originality, clarity of aims and plan, feasibility, and realistic milestones/timescales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: Statement of Qualifications and Career
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must include a Statement of Qualifications and Career as part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to summarise career trajectory and relevant experience; no further formatting guidance given on page — see Scheme Notes for full instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: List of Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of Publications in reverse chronological order – PDF file upload, min. font size Arial 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow formatting instructions exactly (PDF upload, minimum font). The page notes there are no strict rules on number of publications; the overall application is assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: Personal Statement (direct text entry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal Statement – qualifications, research career to date and aspirations. Why will the fellowship be beneficial to you now? – direct text entry of max. 3,500 characters including spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the text in a word processor first and check character count (MS Word: Review → Word Count → 'Characters (with spaces)'). Make a concise, compelling case for your career stage and how the URF will help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: Present salary and salary enhancement details
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter present basic salary and salary enhancement details: provide one figure (which is the total of PRSI + employer’s pension costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an existing TCD employee has queries, contact Payroll. Use the table/figures provided as a guide for SFI Level 3 salaries and on-costs. The 'salary enhancement' figure must be the total on-costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: Research proposal (3-page PDF or plain text)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research proposal: nature of research, including aims and brief plan of the research. Description of methods and techniques, with milestones/timescales. Min. font size Arial 10 and ensure document has a title. (max. 3 page PDF upload / Plain text 12,000 characters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PDF is recommended. References are usually included within the 3 page limit and can be inserted at the end in a slightly smaller font, but ensure they are legible. Keep to the 3-page limit and focus on the central hypothesis, aims, feasibility, and milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: Scientific abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific abstract: direct text entry of max. 1,800 characters (including spaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise summary suitable for reviewers to understand the essence of the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: Animal licence and animal costs fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Several fields for text entry where there are Animal Licence costs. Applications using animals, with TCD as host institution, should include costs to cover Irish Medicine Board project authorisation annual fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the BioResources Unit (provided contact details) for advice on including these costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: Financial details and overheads
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial details: these will be approved by the Research Office in the e-GAP system after you submit. The figure for overheads must be manually entered into the 'Overhead costs/indirect costs' field. The rate is 30% of the total, less equipment costs. ('Estate costs' are not applicable to applicants to Ireland-based institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inputting figures, select 'Duration' (5 years) first to see the full 5-year budget fields. An Excel sheet to assist with Financial Details will be available on RPAMS. Research Office approval is required by stated internal deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: Lay report
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay report: direct text entry of max. 3,500 characters including spaces. Explain why you have chosen to work in this area and what it is about your proposed research that you find particularly exciting, interesting or important. Explain wider potential impact and benefits to society of your proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers place significant importance on this section; make the case in plain language and highlight wider societal impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: Host organisation justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Host organisation justification: Statement justifying your choice of TCD as host institution – direct text entry of max. 1,000 characters (including spaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain specifically why this host is uniquely appropriate for your project and career development (expertise, equipment, environment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: Justification of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification: Fully justify all costs for equipment, travel, consumables, other expenses. – direct text entry of max. 2,000 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, itemised justification tied to the research plan and milestones; reviewers and Research Office will scrutinise cost reasonableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process and internal approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: The application is submitted via the Royal Society’s e-GAP system. The Research Office must approve applications in the system by the RS’ deadline. The normal internal requirement for Head of School sign-off will be fulfilled by the Head of School’s supporting statement which must be provided by the Head of School by the internal deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register in e-GAP early; ensure correct Head of School email to avoid jeopardising the application. See the Submission Process flow diagram in the Scheme Notes for an overview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referees and Head of School responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will be asked to provide contact details of two referees and the Head of School. Heads of School will be asked to provide a short statement (1,000 characters) detailing the applicant’s suitability and intentions for career progression. Two referees should provide confidential references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The onus is on the applicant to advise Head of School and referees of the application well in advance of the supporting-statement deadline and to ensure they know what they need to do (send them Appendix 1 of Scheme Notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal quality: strong and original central hypothesis and clear route to goals
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a strong and original central hypothesis, with a research plan which shows a clear route to a clearly-defined overall goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the significance (big picture) and avoid over-focus on technical minutiae given the 3-page limit. Show feasibility with realistic milestones and timescales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal quality: timeliness, feasibility, balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why your proposed research idea is timely – why now? The research proposal should strike the right balance, be feasible and not over-ambitious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate why the timing is right (methods, opportunities, preliminary data) and show a realistic plan that can achieve its goals within the fellowship period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal quality: preliminary data and domain expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary data should be convincing. Evidence of knowledge of the area, and appropriate experience, should be demonstrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preliminary results to justify feasibility and to strengthen claims about the likelihood of achieving goals; highlight appropriate expertise and prior relevant work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal quality: wider impact to scientific community and society
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to consider and address how the research will affect the wider scientific community and society in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state potential impacts, benefits, and relevance beyond the immediate research question, and reflect these in the lay report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team and collaborators: identify key individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Key individuals should be identified and included as part of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List collaborators and their roles; show how their expertise strengthens feasibility and delivery of the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application practice: get help from senior colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Get help from senior academic colleagues – ask them to read and comment on drafts of the 3-page proposal, personal statement and host organisation justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer feedback improves clarity, scientific argument, and corrects oversights; senior mentors can advise on positioning and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant profile: unique selling point and vision for independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Your USP: How are you, and your set of skills and experience, uniquely placed to solve this research problem? The vision is really important not just in terms of the scientific idea but in terms of becoming an independent researcher – long-term aspirations and where you see yourself in 5 years’ time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate independence through established collaborations, leadership roles (organising conferences, reviewing papers), mentoring, supervision, or other responsibilities. Emphasise plans to achieve independence and future funding/career trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and readability: enthusiasm, clarity, intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be easy to understand and read. It should be a joy to read for the evaluators - the applicant’s enthusiasm and passion for their research should be clearly communicated. Remember the application will be reviewed by working scientists and not experts in the area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clearly, avoid jargon where possible, put the big picture up front, and convey excitement while remaining rigorous. Tailor explanations for reviewers who are competent scientists but not specialists in your narrow subfield.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication record guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: In relation to the publication track record of the applicant, there are no specific guidelines or rules. The assessment would not be based on the publication record alone; it is the overall application combined - the idea, the personal statement, the lay report, etc. that is evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are gaps or fewer publications (e.g., due to commercial sensitivity), explain these circumstances in the application — this will not necessarily count against you if explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching load expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: As the purpose of the URF is to offer the Fellow protected research time, it would not be expected that the fellow would undertake more than ~6 hours of teaching per week (this may increase in later years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If concerned about teaching expectations, contact urf@royalsociety.org for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and post-award expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: URFs must submit annual reports to the Royal Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for annual reporting requirements and plan milestones and outputs accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary research encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Interdisciplinary research is encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise cross-disciplinary elements where relevant and demonstrate appropriate expertise and collaborations across fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to apply for additional funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society actively encourages URF awardees to apply for other awards and grants, once the funding does not cover the URF’s salary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan complementary funding strategies for research activities not fully covered by the URF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biomedical research exclusion and query route
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship applications exclude clinical medicine and any researcher addressing a direct biomedical research question. The scheme no longer supports biomedical research; applicants whose research is biomedical are encouraged to apply to the SFI-HRB-Wellcome Trust Research Career Development fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there is doubt about whether the proposed research addresses a direct biomedical question, the Royal Society will accept queries from applicants who email an abstract to urf@royalsociety.org.
